newsitem.title: CHINA: China B shares end lower, A shares up.
newsitem.headline: China B shares end lower, A shares up.

text.p: China's B shares ended lower on a technical correction in reduced volume on Wednesday, taking a rest after strong rises in recent sessions, brokers said.
A shares rose further on bullish sentiment, they said.
The Shanghai B index fell 0.209 points or 0.24 percent to 86.348 points on volume of 33.694 million shares worth $17.129 million, compared with $26.931 million on Tuesday.
Concerns over companies which are expected to post poor 1996 results limited buying interest, resulting in a correction, brokers said.

"Most investors are waiting for results to be issued in the coming days, which caused a technical correction after the rises of the past few days," one broker said. "But the upward trend will continue."
"Trading volume is shrinking as the index falls, so the correction will be limited," another broker said.
Shanghai Vacuum & Electron Device Company was the biggest loser on profit-taking, slipping $0.024 or 8.57 percent to $0.256 on volume of 1.4 million shares.

Shanghai Industry Sewing Machine Company was the most actively traded on speculative buying by domestic investors amid talk of good dividends, rising $0.022 or 8.57 percent to $2.56 on volume of 2.3 million shares.
The Shenzhen B index lost 1.30 points or 0.73 percent to 177.09 with turnover shrinking to HK$135.4 million from HK$199.4 million on Tuesday.
"Foreign investors seemed to be alarmed by last week's sharp rises and have adopted a wait-and-see attitude," an analyst at China Southern Securities said.
The gap between the B shares and A shares, which have risen substantially in the past few months, will continue to fan buying interest in B shares, analysts said.
The Shenzhen A share index rose 4.61 points or 0.97 percent to 477.80 on turnover of 12.2 billion yuan.
Analysts said they expect the B index to soon break through the historical high of 201.87 points, reached last December, and to maintain the gains over the Hong Kong handover in July.
Anhui Gujing Distillery Co Ltd was the worst B share performer on Wednesday due to investor disappointment over the company's 1996 dividend plan, brokers said.
The company's B shares plunged HK$0.93 or 7.88 percent to end at HK$10.87 on volume of 1.45 million shares.
Gujing has proposed a cash dividend of 0.21 yuan per B share and 0.116 yuan per A share based on 1996 profits, according to the company's 1996 annual report.

The Shanghai A index rose 14.416 points or 1.01 percent to 1,442.618 on volume of 973.6 million shares worth 13.3 billion yuan. The SSE30 blue chip index closed up 63.366 points or 1.72 percent to 3,746.739 points.
